study.title: Scalp acupuncture regulates functional connectivity of cerebral hemispheres in patients with hemiplegia after stroke
study.study_design: Randomized controlled trial with matched healthy controls; resting-state fMRI; two-arm patient comparison plus healthy control group
study.randomization: Patients were randomly classified by using the random number table method
study.population: Patients with left hemiplegia due to ischemic stroke (aged 40-75, right-handed) and matched healthy controls
study.disease_condition: Left hemiplegia due to ischemic stroke (unilateral partial anterior circulation infarction)
study.inclusion_criteria: (a) patients had a clinically diagnosed by computed tomography or MRI first episode of ischemic stroke involving unilateral partial anterior circulation infarction; (b) patients were between 40 and 75 years old and right-handed; (c) patients' course was between 2 weeks and 6 months after the onset of stroke; (d) patients had the stable physical condition without disorders in consciousness or speech and can understand consenting and study-related instructions; (e) patients had signed the informed consent form
study.exclusion_criteria: (a) patients with a course of disease longer than 6 months or in the acute phase of disease progression; (b) patients with sensory aphasia, severe dementia, psychosis, and so on, which may affect the experiment; (c) patients with a cardiac pacemaker, stent, bypass surgery, or otherwise, which were not available for magnetic resonance examination

extraction_notes.note: Table 1 lists SAs n=11 and PCs n=10, but the flow chart (Figure 1) shows scalp acupuncture group n=10 and patient control group n=11. The arm sizes appear to be swapped between these two sources. The correct allocation is unclear from the PDF.
Post-treatment NIHSS scores for each arm are not reported numerically in Table 1 or elsewhere in the text. Only the between-group p-value (p=0.027) after 14 days is reported.
No formal quantitative measure of deqi sensation (e.g., MASS, VAS for deqi components) was reported. Deqi was mentioned only as a target/intended outcome of needle manipulation.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success were not assessed or reported in this study.
Adverse events were not reported in the paper.

Neuroimaging results for the between-group comparison (SAs vs PCs, Figure 4) and some ipsilateral increased RSFC results (Figure 3) are shown only in figures with no coordinate tables provided. Coordinates and statistics for these results could not be extracted.

The paper combines baseline patient groups (SAs and PCs) vs HCs for initial comparisons, but does not specify if these groups were analyzed together or separately. The narrative implies all patients were combined for the HC comparison.

Table 2 Z-values are listed alongside T-values for the SA group post-treatment results; it is unclear whether Z is a separate statistic or a Fisher-transformed correlation coefficient. The paper states 'correlation coefficients were converted to Z values by Fisher conversion' so Z here is likely the Fisher-transformed FC statistic, not a Z-score from a t-distribution.
Trial registration number is not reported anywhere in the manuscript.

The paper does not clearly specify whether the combined patients group (SAs + PCs together) was used for the HC vs patients comparison, or whether SAs and PCs were analyzed separately. The results section describes findings in 'patients' generally relative to HCs without differentiating groups.
Slice thickness for rs-fMRI is reported as 3.5 mm and field of view as 250×250 mm² with matrix 64×64, but explicit voxel size (in-plane resolution) is not stated directly.

The text refers to 'right suboccipital gyrus' in the context of PC results, which may be a translation artifact or non-standard anatomical label (possibly inferior occipital gyrus as labeled in Table 3). Table 3 label 'Inferior occipital gyrus' is likely correct.

The study arm labeled 'SAs' in Table 1 appears to have n=11 participants, but the flow chart labels the scalp acupuncture group as n=10. The SAs group in Table 2 analysis appears to correspond to 10 participants (scalp acupuncture). This discrepancy is unresolved.
